$comment: The support promises: what Mailwoman tells customers it handles. Inside a promise's depth, a wrong parse, a miss or a missing corpus is a bug. Below that depth, the result must be an explicit unresolved component. `country` is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the address is in, `input` the BCP 47 language and script of the typed text, `embeddedNameScripts` the ISO 15924 scripts allowed in a name span inside an otherwise `input`-script address, and `depth` the deepest component guaranteed (one of `SUPPORT_DEPTHS` in packages/codex/lib/support.ts). A promise's evidence is every gauntlet case (packages/mailwoman/tools/eval-harness/gauntlet/cases/) in its country whose letters are all in its input script. The repository check `support-promises` refuses a row whose codes the registry rejects or whose evidence holds no passing case, and reports each failing case inside a promise as an open bug against it. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-14-locale-support-promises-design.md records the design.
